# Jubilees Chapter 36 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Isaac's testament to his sons; division of the inheritance

---

**36:1** In the seventh week, in the first year thereof, in the forty-fifth jubilee, Isaac called his sons Esau and Jacob to him, and they came to him.

**36:2** And he said to them: "My sons, I am going to go the way of all the earth. And this day I divide my inheritance between you two and I give both of you a share.

**36:3** Arise and hear that which I say, that ye may do it, and that ye may not die before your time."

**36:4** "Honour your mother, for she is the mother of you both. And love one another, ye sons; and do not despise one another with your hearts."

**36:5** "Love your brother, and let your hearts not be hostile toward each other, and be not like brothers who hate one another."

**36:6** "And let not the spirit of Mastema rule over you and your seed; let him not bring you into destruction and condemnation."

**36:7** "For I know that Esau will be zealous and angry concerning thee, Jacob, because I have blessed thee; but I command him that he shall do no harm to thee."

**36:8** And he called Esau and said to him: "I am an old man, and behold I am about to die. My eyes are dim and my strength has left me."

**36:9** "Thou hast seen what I gave to Jacob thy brother, and thou hast seen that he has more than thou. And I gave thee much. And I have given both of you an inheritance."

**36:10** "Go now to the mountains of Seir, and thou shalt rule over it. And thou shalt rule from the east to the extremities of Edom. And Jacob shall rule over Canaan and all the land from the river to the sea."

**36:11** "And do not transgress against thy brother Jacob, but do not take away from him his possession. And love him with all thy heart and with all thy soul, and let there be peace between you both."

**36:12** "And if he serve thee faithfully and from a good heart, regard it not as labor, for he is thy brother. And if he serve thee faithfully, it is good. But if thou art found to be treacherous, I will curse thee in my death."

**36:13** And Esau said to him: "I will do all that thou hast commanded me, and I will not transgress against Jacob my brother. He is my brother."

**36:14** And Isaac was pleased at Esau's words and blessed him and said: "The LORD God of Israel bless thee and prosper thy way, and multiply thy seed, and may thy seed possess all that thy heart desireth."

**36:15** And Isaac blessed Jacob and said: "Jacob, my son whom I love, may God bless thee from above, from the dew of heaven and from the dew of the earth."

**36:16** "May God Almighty bless thee and prosper thy way, and let thy seed be many and multiply it."

**36:17** And Isaac called his two sons again, and gave them his testament. And he divided the whole land of Canaan into portions for Jacob, and gave the mountains of Seir to Esau.

**36:18** And he said: "I have given all the land of Canaan to Jacob and to his seed after him forever. And to Esau I have given the mountains of Seir and all that is in them."

**36:19** And after many days Isaac died. And Jacob and Esau buried him at Mamre in the cave of Machpelah, near Abraham their grandfather.

**36:20** And they wept for Isaac greatly — Jacob and Esau — and the whole household wept with them.

---

*EMET notes: Isaac's testament (ch.36) divides the land between Jacob (Canaan) and Esau (Seir) in a formal way that has no equivalent in Genesis. The warning against Mastema (v.6) is Jubilees' distinctive pneumatological framing. The division of the inheritance follows the Jubilees theology of land assignment by divine authority.*
